Clinical practice regarding the management of atrial fibrillation involves critical decisions about the timing of medical interventions. In the context of [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]], the available evidence focuses specifically on the initiation of [[antikoagulationsbehandling]] (anticoagulation treatment). The data reveals a distinct bifurcation in treatment timelines relative to formal diagnosis and hospital discharge [^src1]. 

According to the corpus, 55.6% of patients begin anticoagulation treatment within the four months prior to their official diagnosis, while the remaining 44.4% start treatment within 30 days after hospital discharge [^src1]. This single data point highlights both pre-diagnostic and post-discharge care pathways, though no further details regarding specific clinical guidelines, patient outcomes, or longitudinal trends are available in the current evidence.

## Claims
- Start på antikoagulationsbehandling: 55,6 % af patienterne startede behandlingen inden for 4 måneder før diagnose, mens 44,4 % startede inden for 30 dage efter udskrivelse [^src1] (atrieflimren-i-danmark, antikoagulationsbehandling)
